- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer below forecast mean.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated bullish spikes (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00s), model often fails to capture mean reversion; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >10% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day trend, not 30-day trend.  
- If official events are clustered (e.g., 3+ auctions in 5 days), model overestimates supply impact; reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish but price is rising, model often ignores sentiment; force downward adjustment by 1–3% if sentiment <0.50.  
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply “mean reversion” rule: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×true, for next 5 days.
